items.title: SSA-579716 V1.0: Insufficient Session Expiration Vulnerability in Mendix Runtime
items.summary: The products listed below contain a session management vulnerability that could allow a deactivated user to continue using an existing session to access and modify data within their previously granted permissions. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.

items.title: SSA-545865 V1.0: Improper Token Verification Vulnerability in Mendix OIDC Provider Module
items.summary: Mendix OIDC Provider contains a token verification vulnerability that could allow an remote attack to hijack an Account. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.

items.title: USN-9016-2: Apache HTTP Server regression
items.summary: USN-9016-1 fixed vulnerabilities in Apache2. Unfortunately the upstream fix introduced a regression that prevented cookies being set during a redirect under certain circumstances. This update fixes the problem. Original advisory details: Zhang San, Ankit Prateek, Zhen Kong, SeungHyun Cho, Ryoma Nishioka, Keita Sode and Hyojae Lee discovered that Apache HTTP Server did not correctly handle certain memory operations. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 14.04 LTS, Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04…

items.title: USN-9190-2: Linux kernel (HWE) vulnerabilities
items.summary: Several security issues were discovered in the Linux kernel. An attacker could possibly use these to compromise the system. This update corrects flaws in the following subsystems: - S390 architecture; - x86 architecture; - Block layer subsystem; - Cryptographic API; - Compute Acceleration Framework; - FireWire subsystem; - GPIO subsystem; - GPU drivers; - Microsoft Hyper-V drivers; - I2C subsystem; - Multiple devices driver; - Network drivers; - STMicroelectronics network drivers; - Power supply drivers; - S/390 drivers; - SCSI subsystem; - SPI subsystem; - TCM subsystem; - UFS subsystem; - Fi…

items.title: USN-9209-1: Simple DirectMedia Layer vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Simple DirectMedia Layer incorrectly handled memory when encountering errors during OpenGL ES streaming texture creation. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause applications using Simple DirectMedia Layer to consume resources, resulting in a denial of service.

items.title: USN-9211-1: Plexus Utils vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Plexus Utils did not properly sanitize file paths when extracting archives. If a user or automated system were tricked into extracting a specially crafted archive, an attacker could possibly use this issue to write arbitrary files and execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9208-1: alsa-lib vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that the ALSA library incorrectly handled certain crafted topology files and control element identifiers. An attacker could possibly use these issues to cause a denial of service or expose sensitive information. These issues were only addressed in Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.

items.title: USN-9207-1: Apache Commons BCEL vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Apache Commons BCEL incorrectly cached classes under their self-declared names without validating them against the requested name. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause BCEL to return or verify a different class than the one requested.

items.title: USN-9204-1: dav1d vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that dav1d incorrectly handled certain AV1 video streams with extremely large frame sizes. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause dav1d to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9198-1: HTTP::Tiny vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that HTTP::Tiny incorrectly forwarded credential headers supplied by the caller, such as Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization, when following cross-origin redirects, including redirects from HTTPS to HTTP. An attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information.

items.title: USN-9201-1: NetworkManager vulnerability
items.summary: Juthawong Naisanguansee discovered that NetworkManager on Ubuntu incorrectly granted the whoopsie user unrestricted D-Bus access to root-only methods. A local attacker who can execute code as the whoopsie user could possibly use this issue to disrupt system networking or alter NetworkManager logging and connection configurations.

items.title: Investigation underway into DWP cyber incident as services taken offline
items.summary: The UK’s largest government department, the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), has taken services offline following a cyber incident. DWP, which administers disability and health benefits, state pensions and child maintenance payments, said it was working with government cyber security specialists to assess the incident. items.title: Young British men lose £11bn in the ‘Moneysphere’
items.summary: Nearly half of young men in the UK have lost a combined total of £11bn through investment scams pitched to them via social media, a survey commissioned by Starling Bank has found. According to the survey of over 2,000 Gen Z males in the UK, aged between 14 and 29, 44% have fallen for these scams. Over two million Gen Z men in the UK fell victim to investment scams with an average of just over £5,000 lost, taking the total to about £11bn. items.title: NCSC-2026-0525 [1.00] [M/H] Kwetsbaarheden verholpen in Linux kernel
items.summary: De Linux kernel ontwikkelaars hebben meerdere kwetsbaarheden verholpen in diverse subsystemen en drivers, waaronder IPv6, KVM, SUNRPC, NFS, SMB, XFS, overlayfs, OCFS2, media drivers, netwerkdrivers, geheugenbeheer, en meer. items.title: NCSC-2026-0524 [1.00] [H/H] Kwetsbaarheid verholpen in Drupal core
items.summary: Drupal heeft een nieuwe kwetsbaarheid verholpen in Drupal core, specifiek in het install.php bestand en in versies tot 10.6.23 en van 11.0.0 tot 11.4.14. Het install.php bestand bevatte kwetsbaarheden die konden leiden tot overname van de site indien het bestand toegankelijk bleef na de SA-CORE-2026-017 advisory, warvoor het NCSC de eerdere advisory NCSC-2026-0507 heeft gepubliceerd. November 2026 einen unberechtigten Zugriff auf die Shopsysteme. Die Ursache ist unbekannt. Der Händler trennte die Systemverbindungen und schaltete den Shop in den Wartungsmodus. Damit sei der Zugriff beendet gewesen. Er deaktivierte alle Kundenpasswörter vorsorglich, setzte weitere Sicherheitsmaßnahmen um und informierte die Datenschutzaufsicht. items.title: Sicherheitsvorfall - Bell Canada
items.summary: Der kanadische Telekommunikationsanbieter Bell Canada bestätigte, dass ein Angreifer am 17. November 2026 in seine Systeme eindrang und Daten von Firmenkunden stahl. Bell nennt den Täter "agentic", was auf den Einsatz von KI-Werkzeugen deutet. Der Angreifer griff auf mehrere Systeme zu, darunter eine Vorproduktionsumgebung des Systems Maximo. Bell nutzt es, um Netzverbindungen zu bestellen und bereitzustellen. Betroffen sind Geschäftskontakte mit Namen, Positionen, E-Mail-Adressen, Telefonnummern und Geschäftsanschriften. items.title: People are willing to pay to vanish from search results
items.summary: More than half of U.S. adults would like to see a log of everyone who has searched for their name online. In a survey of 1,008 adults by Incogni, 53% said they would like that record to cover the past five years, and 55% said they would pay to have their personal information permanently removed from all public search results. “You can learn an extraordinary amount about someone without ever speaking to them. items.title: kernel: vdpa_sim_blk: reject out-of-range sector starts
items.summary: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's vDPA vHost Data Path Acceleration block simulator driver. Due to improper input validation, the driver logs out-of-range starting sector requests but fails to reject them, causing an arithmetic underflow and an invalid buffer offset. An attacker with access to the simulated device, such as a guest virtual machine, can submit a crafted storage request to trigger out-of-bounds memory reads and writes in the host kernel. This flaw may result in a system crash leading to a denial of service, information disclosure, or arbitrary code execution...

items.summary: Bypass URL Parser A tool that tests MANY URL bypasses to reach a 4xx-protected page. If you wonder why this code is nothing but a dirty curl wrapper, here's why: Most Python HTTP clients perform URL/path/parameter encoding and decoding, and I hate this. If I submit raw chars, I want raw chars to be sent. If I send a weird path, I want it weird, not normalized. items.title: I'll Have a Raw JSON, Please: Leaking a LangChain Assistant Through Format Coercion
items.summary: A guardrail written in the system prompt reads the question, not the answer. During a red team exercise, a customer's support assistant refused every direct question about itself and never gave up its system prompt. Yet asking for raw JSON instead of prose turned its internal state into a reply: tool calls and their arguments, retrieved documents with their metadata, and the output of its safety classifier. We show how it works, why the framework is not at fault, and why filtering the output is the only fix that holds.

items.title: Namespace Filtering in Icinga for Kubernetes: How We Built It
items.summary: Icinga for Kubernetes synchronizes every namespace in a cluster. Starting with version 0.5.0, you can change that: a new namespaces option takes either a list of namespaces to include, or a list of namespaces to exclude. I expected a quick config option and a filter in the sync. It turned out the Kubernetes API doesn’t offer what you would want here. This post explains how namespace filtering works and why we built it the way we did. What does the configuration look like? You set exactly one of two lists in config.yml. items.title: From one IOC to a repeatable investigation with MispQL
items.summary: A teammate sends you a domain as an indicator of compromise (IOC) and asks whether it has shown up in your threat intelligence. You find a few related observations, then the questions get more specific. Which results belong to the same domain family? Which MISP events contain them? How many matching records have changed in the last day? Can the next analyst run the same search?
